relevance_note: Single case report of a woman with a GFAP variant and Alexander disease: "resulting in known pathogenic heterozygous p.Arg70Trp variant".
method_note: Hand extraction of a single-patient case report (no tables); output assembled by a short Python script in scratch, spans sliced to match the paper's thin spaces in 'c.208C > T'. Label 'patient' (rule 5). 'Neither postural instability, nor ataxia was checked, while brisk reflexes were present' read as absence (contrasted with 'present'); this wording could also mean not examined. Brisk lower-limb reflexes recorded as a pyramidal sign for the checklist; mild cognitive impairment recorded as cognitive decline. Age 58 is the age at presentation; she was followed for 18 months afterwards, so age at last evaluation is the presentation age. Age at onset not stated as an age (tremor began '4 months ago'). Vital status not stated explicitly (follow-up ongoing 'until now'). Checklist 'basal ganglia or thalamic abnormality' left not reported: MRI states 'no abnormal change in basal ganglia' (narrower than the composite item, thalamus not addressed) while FP-CIT PET shows severe striatal dopaminergic depletion. Checklist 'cerebral white matter abnormality' and 'periventricular rim' left not reported: only 'No major lesions in ... periventricular white matter' (figure legend) is stated, which is narrower/qualified. 'Routine laboratory work ups were unremarkable' recorded as written (excludes nothing more specific). 'This patient did not have typical symptoms suggestive of Alexander disease' not used to exclude any specific checklist item. Variant type not stated by authors (not derived from HGVS). Family history negative, but no parental testing reported, so inheritance not reported. No contradictions found.
